definitions.explanation: The salty taste quality or the amount of salt in food.

examples.japanese: このスープは{塩気|しおけ}が{足|た}りない。
examples.english: This soup doesn't have enough salt.

examples.japanese: {塩気|しおけ}が{強|つよ}すぎて{喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}く。
examples.english: It's too salty and makes me thirsty.

examples.japanese: {健康|けんこう}のために{塩気|しおけ}を{控|ひか}えめにしている。
examples.english: I'm keeping the salt content low for my health.

notes:
FORMATION:
{塩|しお} (salt) + {気|け} (quality/presence of)

The {気|け} suffix indicates the presence or quality of something.

COLLOCATIONS:
・{塩気|しおけ}が{足|た}りない - not salty enough
・{塩気|しおけ}が{強|つよ}い - too salty
・{塩気|しおけ}を{控|ひか}える - to reduce salt
・{塩気|しおけ}のある - having saltiness

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{塩味|しおあじ} - salty taste (also means salty flavor)
・{塩分|えんぶん} - salt content (more technical)

USAGE:
{塩気|しおけ} is more commonly used in everyday cooking contexts, while {塩分|えんぶん} is used in health/nutrition contexts.
